pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. I read the tests but could not run them.
The item() helper in src/index.js omits the label for normal. The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact <li> texts.
The query uses WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id. The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal, including id order (items 3 and 1 set to high).
The unfiltered query keeps ORDER BY id. The 'AC-4' test asserts all items in order.
nav() renders <strong> for the current filter and links for the others. The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views. The 400 response has no nav, which fits the spec.

src/index.js returns 400 when the parameter is present and not in the set; the empty value is also rejected. The 'AC-6' test covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks that there is no <li>.

src/index.js picks the message from a COUNT of the table. The 'AC-7' test asserts the exact messages for high, low and normal with no match, and 'No items yet.' in all four views with an empty table. The later 'No match' state test was loosened, but AC-7 still has its own strong test.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it, and scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts a query.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe('No low-priority items.') to toBeDefined(). message() returns null or a string, never undefined, so the assertion can never fail. The test no longer checks the filter's own message. The 'AC-7' test still covers the exact messages, but the spec does not justify loosening this test.
The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened the 'No match' assertion in test/priority.test.js. The claim is false.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion and keep the claim, or disclose the loosening and its reason.

findings.what: The PR does not mention the new tests added to tests/traffic-config.test.sh for fragment and space routes, or that '?' is now allowed in the route check.
findings.fix: Say so in the engineering details (the 'Traffic route check' bullet already covers part of it).

lenses.note: A spec exists; all items are implemented as written, with no extra behaviour beyond the traffic-check change the PR discloses.
The decisions (existing items normal, only high and low labelled) are followed.
One assertion in the 'No match' state test was loosened to a vacuous toBeDefined(). The other tests assert exact behaviour. I could not run the suite: vitest is not installed in the sandbox.
The README describes the new filter. CLAUDE.md conventions are followed: the migration is additive and the traffic route is added.
No defects found. The query is parameterised, the input is whitelisted and titles are HTML-escaped.
The priority value is validated against a whitelist and bound as a SQL parameter. Output is escaped. No injected instructions were found in the repo content.
The change adds a nav and list markup, but there is no stylesheet or UI framework, and the PR gives no screenshots.
No browser or UI flow was available to demonstrate; the page is server-rendered HTML covered by tests.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false.
